subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represents a pair of straight lines, show that the angle θ between the two lines is given by cos θ = ±(a + b) / √((a − b)² + 4h²).

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
Write tan θ from the two slopes
Put the sum and product into tan θ
Convert tan θ to cos θ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 4 PAIR OF STRAIGHT LINES, Short Answer question 2, book p.163. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The split is 1+1+1+1 because this proof turns four times and each turn is a separate piece of knowledge: splitting the pair into slopes, the angle formula in slopes, the identity that converts the difference of the slopes into the sum and the product, and the conversion from tan to cos. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what you know about the two slopes, and how you get from tan θ to cos θ.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. A homogeneous second-degree equation is two lines through the origin, so each line is y = mx. Matching coefficients gives the sum and the product of the two slopes — never the slopes themselves.
steps.memory_tip: Matching coefficients gives the SUM and the PRODUCT of the slopes, never the slopes one by one.
lines: Let the two lines be y = m₁x and y = m₂x, b ≠ 0.
Then ax² + 2hxy + by² ≡ b(y − m₁x)(y − m₂x)
On equating like term coeff., we get

recall.must_convey: That the pair is split as b(y − m₁x)(y − m₂x), giving m₁ + m₂ = −2h/b and m₁m₂ = a/b.
accept: split the pair into two lines through the origin and equate coefficients
the sum of the slopes is minus two h over b and the product is a over b
write the pair as b into y minus m one x into y minus m two x
slopes sum and product teesukovali
match the coefficients of x squared and x y

steps.why: Every proof in this chapter starts by SPLITTING the pair into two lines with unknown slopes and matching coefficients. The link it gives between (a, h, b) and the two slopes is what every later step uses.
common_mistakes: Writing m₁ + m₂ = 2h/b without the minus sign.
Dividing by a instead of b.

steps.label: Write tan θ from the two slopes
steps.margin_note: One mark. Two lines meeting at a point make two angles, θ and 180° − θ, whose tangents are opposite in sign — that is where the ± comes from, and it stays to the end.
steps.memory_tip: Two lines make two angles, θ and 180° − θ, so the ± is there from the start.
lines: θ is the angle between the two lines, so

recall.must_convey: That tan θ = ±(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂) and that (m₁ − m₂)² = (m₁ + m₂)² − 4m₁m₂.
accept: tan theta is the difference of the slopes over one plus their product
the plus or minus is because the lines make two angles
the difference squared is the sum squared minus four times the product
tan theta formula raasi difference ni sum and product tho rayali
use the standard angle between two lines formula
heard_as: one plus m one m two

steps.why: Only the sum and the product of the slopes are known, so any expression in the slopes must first be written through those two. The identity in the third line is what makes the difference of the slopes reachable.

steps.label: Put the sum and product into tan θ
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both the numerator and the denominator carry a factor 1/b, so those two factors cancel and the result is in a, h and b only.
steps.memory_tip: Numerator and denominator each carry a factor 1/b, so those two factors cancel.

recall.must_convey: That substituting (1) gives m₁ − m₂ = ±2√(h² − ab)/b and 1 + m₁m₂ = (a + b)/b, so tan θ = ±2√(h² − ab)/(a + b).
accept: substitute the sum and the product from one
the difference of the slopes is two root h squared minus a b over b
one plus the product is a plus b over b
sum and product substitute chesthe b cancel avuthundi
tan theta is two root h squared minus a b over a plus b
heard_as: root h squared minus a b

steps.why: The quantity h² − ab decides everything about the pair: it is positive for two separate lines, zero for two coincident lines and negative when there are no real lines at all.
common_mistakes: Cancelling only one of the two b factors.

steps.label: Convert tan θ to cos θ
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Read tan θ as opposite over adjacent, so the hypotenuse is √(p² + q²) and cos θ is adjacent over hypotenuse. The 4h² and the −4ab combine with (a + b)² to give (a − b)² + 4h².
steps.memory_tip: tan θ = p/q gives cos θ = q/√(p² + q²) — read the fraction as opposite over adjacent.
lines: If tan θ = p/q then cos θ = q/√(p² + q²)
Here p = 2√(h² − ab) and q = a + b

recall.must_convey: That p² + q² = (a − b)² + 4h², so cos θ = ±(a + b)/√((a − b)² + 4h²).
accept: if tan theta is p over q then cos theta is q over root p squared plus q squared
p squared plus q squared works out to a minus b whole squared plus four h squared
the minus four a b turns the plus two a b into minus two a b
tan nunchi cos ki marchali, hypotenuse root p square plus q square
this gives the required result
heard_as: root p squared plus q squared

steps.why: The −4ab from the numerator turns the +2ab inside (a + b)² into −2ab, which is exactly what makes (a − b)² appear. The result also reads correctly when a + b = 0: cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°, the known condition for a perpendicular pair.
common_mistakes: Writing cos θ = p/√(p² + q²), which is sin θ.
Leaving (a + b)² under the root instead of (a − b)².
